You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From f46f156ea7704a40577800c3df63b599121a87ec Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2017 17:46:52 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915/selftests: Only touch archdata.iommu when it exists

archdata.iommu only exists when CONFIG_IOMMU_API is enabled (and only
applies to intel-iommu in our case) so conditionally compile it out when
it doesn't exist.

Fixes: b5891fb520f7 ("drm/i915/selftests: Disable iommu for the mock device")
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Matthew Auld <matthew.auld@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20170918164652.14200-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk
Reviewed-by: Matthew Auld <matthew.auld@intel.com>
---
 drivers/gpu/drm/i915/selftests/mock_gem_device.c | 2 ++
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+)

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/selftests/mock_gem_device.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/selftests/mock_gem_device.c
index 38ed006be5be..2388424a14da 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/selftests/mock_gem_device.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/selftests/mock_gem_device.c
@@ -146,8 +146,10 @@ struct drm_i915_private *mock_gem_device(void)
 	dev_set_name(&pdev->dev, "mock");
 	dma_coerce_mask_and_coherent(&pdev->dev, DMA_BIT_MASK(32));
 
+#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IOMMU_API)
 	/* hack to disable iommu for the fake device; force identity mapping */
 	pdev->dev.archdata.iommu = (void *)-1;
+#endif
 
 	dev_pm_domain_set(&pdev->dev, &pm_domain);
 	pm_runtime_enable(&pdev->dev);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the code attempting to access `archdata.iommu` without checking if it exists, which only happens when the `CONFIG_IOMMU_API` configuration option is enabled. This led to potential compilation issues or runtime errors when the IOMMU API was not available, as the code would try to manipulate a non-existent member of the structure. The patch fixes this by conditionally compiling the code that accesses `archdata.iommu`, ensuring it only runs when the IOMMU API is enabled.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the code attempting to access `archdata.iommu` without checking if it exists, which only happens when the `CONFIG_IOMMU_API` configuration option is enabled. This led to potential compilation issues or runtime errors when the IOMMU API was not available, as the code would try to manipulate a non-existent member of the structure. The patch fixes this by conditionally compiling the code that accesses `archdata.iommu`, ensuring it only runs when the IOMMU API is enabled.
